handled_verified.note: THIRTY-FOUR types, each read in src/ast/real-svelte-analyzer.ts and each pinned. `ERROR` and `MISSING` are here on CORPUS MEASUREMENT, and they are the two types that made this lane's section A red — both sat in no bucket, which is silence, and for html and toml silence was the right answer. It is not the right answer here, and the precedent had to be set aside to see it. Over 410 sampled files of the 6,143-file corpus, 10 files (2.44%) carry recovery nodes: 55 ERROR nodes and 5 MISSING nodes, every MISSING being the grammar's expected `>` tag terminator. Eight of twelve deliberately malformed documents also produce ERROR, so the path is reachable by hand as well as by corpus. html ruled MISSING INTERNAL SILENT after twelve malformed documents produced none, and toml ruled both silent because the grammar never emits them; applying either ruling to svelte would have been copying a conclusion whose measurement had not been run. The analyzer reads both at the node's OWN span and reports `Syntax <type> detected. The Brain Engine is bypassing this broken node`, alongside the engine's own parse diagnostic — two messages per site, both wanted: the analyzer says what it skipped, the engine says what failed to parse. The read initially covered `ERROR` but NOT `MISSING`, because the walk iterated `namedChild` and the expected `>` is an ANONYMOUS node; the engine's walk uses `children` and did report it, so nothing was lost operationally, but the contract was honoured for one recovery type and silently not the other. Fixed by matching the engine's walk. Pinned by `svelte/error-recovery` and the mutant `svelte/recovery-stops-walk`. That fixture arranges the damage so it cannot be faked: an unclosed `{#if}` makes the parser's ERROR span swallow the REST OF THE FILE, so valid markup sits inside the error region, and a walk that stopped at the recovery node would publish the module, `shared` and one component at L7 and then nothing — while the document still looked analysed, because the module symbol spans the whole root. That truncation is the defect class no count-based gate here can see.

gap._description: Confirmed missing emissions (probe-verified against the real WASM)

gaps.missing: template expressions emit NO references to the component's own members — {count}, label={label}, {#each items as item} (collection), {#await promise then value}, {@html raw}, {@const x = items.length}, {@debug items}, <svelte:component this={Comp}> all read script-side state but zero Uses/references edges are emitted. Only on: directives (calls) and {@render} (calls) produce edges; the template<->script data-flow is otherwise entirely silent.
gaps.evidence:
probe: {count} + + {#each items as item}

{item}

{/each} + {#await promise then value}

{value}

{/await} + {@html raw} -> only instantiates for MyButton; zero edges to count/label/items/promise/raw
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (svelte/template-member-uses) + mutants svelte/drop-template-member-uses + svelte/reemit-shadowed-uses CAUGHT (2026-08-27). Template expressions ({count}, label={label}, {#each items as item}, {#await promise then value}, {@html raw}, {@const total}, {@debug x}, <svelte:component this={Comp}>) emit Uses edges (isTemplateExpression) to member symbols. Scope collision coverage is extended by S5: each-loop and declaration-order-aware {@const} shadowing is separately pinned by svelte/each-shadow-collision.

gaps.missing: let { a, b } = $props() double-declares each binding — extractSvelteDeclarations emits Property symbols (isSvelteProp/fromRunes, component-owned) AND the JS sub-analyzer's destructured Variable symbols (isConst/isDestructured, unowned) both survive the merge. Every rune-prop binding appears twice with conflicting kinds/ownership, polluting symbol consumers.
gaps.evidence: probe: let { a, b } = $props() -> a: 2x (property owner=comp [isSvelteProp,fromRunes] | variable owner=- [isConst,isDestructured]); same for b
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (svelte/rune-props-dedupe expectSymbolCount == 1) + mutant svelte/reduplicate-rune-props CAUGHT (2026-08-27). $props() destructured bindings (let { a, b, c = 5 } = $props()) are now declared EXACTLY once as component-owned Properties; the JS sub-analyzer's parallel destructured Variables are dropped during the merge.

gaps.missing: template-local each-loop and {@const} bindings that collide with same-named component members leaked false template Uses edges. {#each rows as row} and nested {#each ... as item} read local values, not member functions; {@const total = ...} is local to its enclosing block and must shadow the member only after its declaration.
gaps.evidence: probe + fixture: members row/item/total colliding with {#each rows as row}, nested {#each ... as item}, and {@const total = ...}; pre-fix emitted false uses -> row/item/total; post-fix svelte/each-shadow-collision passes and the scope-order probe preserves a legitimate use before the const declaration while suppressing later local reads
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (svelte/each-shadow-collision) + focused mutant svelte/reemit-shadowed-member-uses CAUGHT. Lexical template scopes now share state among siblings for declaration-order-aware {@const} bindings, isolate nested blocks, and register each-loop variables; no false member Uses remain for the tested collision shapes.

gaps.missing: the same reactive state variable assigned by multiple `$:` blocks was emitted once per block, and the JS/TS sub-analyzer's plain declaration survived alongside the Svelte-owned reactive symbol, producing duplicate symbols and ambiguous containment.
gaps.evidence: probe + fixture: reactive-dedupe pre-fix emitted doubled three times and total twice; post-fix expectSymbolCount equals 1 for doubled, total, and count
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (svelte/reactive-dedupe) + focused mutant svelte/reduplicate-reactive-targets CAUGHT. Reactive targets are deduplicated within Svelte extraction and the sub-analyzer copy is dropped in favor of the component-owned reactive symbol.

gaps.missing: shorthand attributes `<Comp {value} />` parse as attribute with the whole `{value}` as the NAME (no expression child), so no walk ever visited them — the most idiomatic Svelte 5 prop-passing shape emitted no use.
gaps.evidence: probe S-shorthand-attr: pre-fix uses=[] for member value; post-fix uses=value. Rejected-shape guard: named attributes WITH an expression child stay on the generic expression path (no double collection).
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (svelte/template-attr-shapes expects uses value) + mutant svelte/drop-attr-shape-uses CAUGHT (2026-09-11). Attribute-name scan collects {value} into templateExprNames for the same member-resolved Uses emission as every other template read.

gaps.missing: bare `this={X}` values were never read, so dynamic component targets were invisible. Member-bound targets (this={fn}) already flowed through the generic expression path as Uses; import-bound targets had no edge at all.
gaps.evidence: probe S-dynamic-this: pre-fix zero edges to imported Comp; post-fix instantiates Comp. Member-bound this={currentView} keeps exactly one Uses edge (no double emission) per the attr probe.
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (svelte/template-attr-shapes expects instantiates DynComp + uses currentView, forbids instantiates currentView) + mutant svelte/drop-dynamic-this-instantiates CAUGHT (2026-09-11). Import-bound bare identifiers in component position resolve post-merge to instantiates (static-<Comp/> semantics); member-resolved targets keep their 3c Uses only.

gaps.missing: `<Comp {...props} />` carries the whole spread expression in the attribute NAME with no expression child — member use for props was never emitted. Full key expansion would be constant evaluation (out of scope); the spread argument reads as one use.
gaps.evidence: probe S-spread-attr: pre-fix uses=[] for member props; post-fix uses=props.
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (svelte/template-attr-shapes expects uses props) + mutant svelte/drop-attr-shape-uses CAUGHT (2026-09-11). Spread arguments are stripped of `...` and collected through the same char-walk tokenizer as every other template read.

gaps.missing: script-derived ranges were half-mapped: symbols shifted lines (columns only when starting on the script's first line, indices never); imports shifted lines only; exports and errors were pushed fully raw. Same disease class as Vue H2/H3, wider (all three dimensions on errors).
gaps.evidence: probe S-script-ranges: pre-fix helper range startIndex script-relative (1); post-fix SFC-absolute (20) with SFC line/column. Engine already supplied sfcScriptStartIndex (Vue wave); the analyzer now consumes it.
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (svelte/script-range-coherence pins work startLine 4/startColumn 1/startIndex 50/endIndex 86 via expectSymbolRanges, the first user of that gate class) + mutant svelte/script-relative-indices CAUGHT (2026-09-11). offsetRange mirrors the Vue contract (single-line endColumn rule, guarded index shifts); sub-symbol/import/error loops shift lines + first-line columns + byte indices.

gaps.missing: the then/catch seeding appended a phantom literal entry shadowing identifier x in EVERY await block subtree, so a real member x read inside any await block emitted nothing — over-shadowing by hardcoded hack.
gaps.evidence: probe S-await-x-shadow / S2-await-block-x: pre-fix member x suppressed; post-fix uses x alongside promise. Empty blocks already collect nothing, so the hack was pure harm.
gaps.closure: CLOSED — phantom entry deleted; fixture-gated (svelte/await-inline-shadow expects uses x read inside the await block alongside the M4 pins) + mutant svelte/readd-phantom-x-shadow CAUGHT (2026-09-11). Empty blocks already collect nothing, so the hack was pure harm.

gaps.missing: the flat identifier regex read string contents as member reads: f("a=b") emitted Uses(a) + Uses(b) alongside the real f (Vue D1 analog, unshared code).
gaps.evidence: probe S2-string-contents / S-const-eq-string: pre-fix a+b emitted for f("a=b")/f("x"); post-fix only f. Backtick ${...} re-enters code (brace-tracked); backslash escapes honored.
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (svelte/template-string-safety expects uses f, forbids uses a/b with same-named members present) + mutant svelte/reemit-string-content-uses CAUGHT (2026-09-11). Char-walk tokenizer with quote states implements the Vue D1/M1 contract locally.

gaps.missing: member-chain leaves misattributed: user.name emitted Uses(name) alongside Uses(user) when a member shared the leaf name (Vue M1 analog). Dotted callee leaves and ?./#-preceded tokens skipped as receivers.
gaps.evidence: probe S2-member-chain: pre-fix name emitted for {user.name} with member name present; post-fix only user.
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (svelte/template-string-safety expects uses user, forbids uses name with member name present) + mutant svelte/reemit-chain-leaf-uses CAUGHT (2026-09-11). Receiver-only emission inside the same char-walk as M2.

gaps.missing: `{#await promise then value}` / `as d` (no explicit block node) never registered the inline vars as template-locals, so {value}/{d} leaked as false member uses — companion to M1 (block form over-shadowed, inline form under-shadowed).
gaps.evidence: probe S3-inline-await-value: pre-fix uses value leaked (and the malformed-probe incident — missing {/await} parses with no await_statement at all, fixed in the probe, documented in #736); post-fix uses promise only. Both then and as spellings covered.
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (svelte/await-inline-shadow expects uses promise+data, forbids uses value+d with same-named members present, both then and as spellings) + mutant svelte/reemit-inline-await-uses CAUGHT (2026-09-11; the value half additionally covered by svelte/reemit-shadowed-uses).

gaps.missing: module-block exports were pushed raw with script-relative ranges — the H4 wave shifted symbols/imports/errors but missed the export push. Same disease, one loop.
gaps.evidence: probe D1-module-export-ranges: pre-fix VERSION at startLine 2/startIndex 14 (script-relative); post-fix SFC line 3/index 50.
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (svelte/module-block-exports gains expectExportRanges pinning VERSION at SFC line 2/columns 14-21/indices 39-46, the first user of that new gate class) + mutant svelte/script-relative-export-ranges CAUGHT (2026-09-11).

gaps.missing: the template char-walk had no comment states: `{f(a) /* b */}` read member b, multi-line `{url // pick}` read member pick. D2 (aliased this=) probed clean in the same battery — items carry local names.
gaps.evidence: probes D3-comment-contents / D3-line-comment: pre-fix uses b/pick alongside real reads; post-fix only real reads. Comment skipping runs in code context only, so '//' inside string literals stays literal.
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (svelte/template-comment-safety: block + line comments with adversarial same-named members) + mutant svelte/reemit-comment-uses CAUGHT (2026-09-11). Family follow-up flagged: Vue's twin machine has the same hole, fixed here where probe-proven.

gaps.missing: `{@render helpers.row(it)}` resolved to the FIRST segment (calls helpers — a namespace object, never callable) while on: dotted handlers resolve to the LAST (`box.open` -> open). Same shape, opposite answers.
gaps.evidence: probe D4-render-dotted: pre-fix calls helpers; post-fix calls row with children?.() fallback intact. F5 oracle mirror updated in lockstep (M37.21 protocol).
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (svelte/template-calls gains the dotted render case: expects row, forbids helpers) + mutant svelte/render-first-segment-calls CAUGHT (2026-09-11). Callable leaf = last all-identifier segment; non-conforming shapes keep the leading-identifier fallback.

gaps.missing: {#if cond}, {:else if cond} and {#key exp} heads carry opaque svelte_raw_text with no `expression` node — nothing ever collected them. Every earlier fixture masked the hole because each condition member was ALSO read elsewhere; isolated conditions emitted zero edges.
gaps.evidence: probes D5-if-only / D5-else-if-key-only + MECH dump (if_start->[block_start_tag, svelte_raw_text]): pre-fix uses=[] for condition-only members; post-fix all read. Pure reads, no bindings (unlike each/await).
gaps.closure: CLOSED — fixture-gated fix (svelte/template-condition-uses: if-only, else-if and key-only reads) + mutant svelte/drop-condition-uses CAUGHT (2026-09-11).

gaps.node_type: call_expression (identifier as the RECEIVER of a method call)
gaps.missing: A `uses` edge is LOST whenever the identifier being read is the RECEIVER of a method call. `$: header = title.toUpperCase()` emits no `uses -> title`, while `$: o = title.length` and `$: o = fn(title)` both emit theirs, and the same expression without the `$:` (`o = title.toUpperCase()`) also loses it. Isolated by A/B on one line of input: property access survives, a call ARGUMENT survives, a call RECEIVER does not. The shape is common in real components -- `items.slice()`, `data.map()`, `value.trim()`, `el.focus()` -- so this is a whole class of under-claimed edges, not a one-off.
gaps.evidence: NOT A SVELTE DEFECT. The svelte analyzer delegates its <script> block to the javascript/typescript sub-analyzer, and a plain `.js` file reproduces it exactly: `const o = title.toUpperCase()` -> no `uses -> title`, while `const o = title.length` and `const o = fn(title)` -> both present. svelte INHERITS the behaviour, so the fix belongs to the javascript lane and the M12 fixture `Card.svelte` shows the real cost: it declares `export let title` at L4 and reads it at L14 in `$: header = title.toUpperCase()`, and no edge is produced. OWNER: the javascript lane, which is under active parallel work — deliberately NOT fixed here, because editing another lane's live code to make this lane's gate green is the failure mode this project keeps naming. WHY IT IS NOT IN THE M12 TRUTH: stating the missing edge as a truth fact would make the gate permanently red on a defect this lane does not own, so it is tracked here instead — the same treatment the `#914` implements residual and the go separator retraction received.
gaps.status: OPEN — CROSS-LANE, owner is the javascript analyzer
gaps.closure: Closes when the javascript analyzer emits a `uses` edge for the receiver of a dotted call. Re-test with the A/B above; the svelte M12 fixture then needs one added fact (`uses Card -> title` at L14) and precision stays 1.000.

gaps.node_type: new_expression (anonymous class expression) — ORACLE defect, TypeScript side
gaps.missing: The TYPESCRIPT oracle's `new_expression` branch derives its constructor target from `ctor.text` with no nameability guard, so an ANONYMOUS class expression publishes raw source text as a name. Measured, not inferred: `validator/samples/inline-new-class/input.svelte` contains `const a = new class { foo = $state(0) }`; the typescript grammar yields `new_expression` with `ctor.type === "class"` and `ctor.text` equal to the whole `class {\n\t\tfoo = $state(0)\n\t}` body, and the oracle emits `instantiates -> 'class { ... }'`. A target that is a span of source text is the same class the TOML lane recorded as an unresolvable identity, and here it is produced by the TRUTH side, which is worse: a differential charges the analyzer for the oracle's mistake.
gaps.evidence: THE JAVASCRIPT ORACLE ALREADY HAS THE GUARD THIS ONE LACKS, at deriveJavaScriptEdges' `new_expression` branch: it restricts candidates to nameable leaves (identifier / member_expression / qualified_identifier / template_type / generic_type / type_identifier / type_descriptor / primitive_type) and its comment records the exact reason — deriving raw expression text `fabricated unmatchable oracle edges (lodash corpus)`. The typescript twin, which this same file describes as carrying the same contract, was never hardened. WHY THE JAVASCRIPT GRAMMAR NEVER HIT IT: on this input the javascript grammar produces NO `new_expression` at all, so the JS oracle is never asked the question — which is precisely how a twin drifts from its twin. THE FIX, for the owner, is the JS guard applied to the TS branch at the `new_expression` case: require `ctor.type` to be a nameable leaf before reading `ctor.text` as a name, and drop the edge otherwise. An anonymous class expression has no honest target name. OWNER: the typescript oracle, in `script/m14/differential.ts` — a file under active parallel edit, so this is recorded rather than changed from the svelte lane, on the same reasoning as X1. IMPACT ON THIS LANE, stated so the number is not misread: svelte's differential at 1,000 files per corpus is 99.7-99.9% with `MISSING` equal to exactly this shape, and `unexplained` 0-2. The svelte ANALYZER does not produce the bad edge and does not miss a real one on this evidence; the single MISSING is the truth side's defect. Until it is fixed, svelte's depth figure cannot be 100%, and reporting it as 100% would mean quietly excluding the one disagreement that exists.
gaps.status: OPEN — CROSS-LANE, owner is the typescript oracle
gaps.closure: Closes when the TS `new_expression` branch refuses a non-nameable constructor. Re-test with `--lang svelte --sample 1000`, which should then read MISSING=0 on both corpora. Note the figure ROTATES between runs because the sample is a rotation: one run read 2 MISSING / 0 unexplained and the next 1 MISSING / 2 unexplained, so a single run is not evidence of stability either way.

decisions.question: Are member-call runes call edges?
decisions.ruling: NO — language keywords. The analyzer gates on isRuneCallee(FULL callee text): $-prefixed callees whose leaf is in RUNE_LEAF_SEGMENTS are suppressed. The F5 oracle previously matched only the bare LEAF target so $derived.by surfaced as fake MISSING 'by'/'pre' (4 in the svelte repo lane); the oracle now mirrors isRuneCallee on the carried fullCallee text. fixture: rune-call-filter (forbids by/root/state).
decisions.resolution: RULED — YES, a call edge (2026-09-27). A rune that INVOKES its argument turns a named function reference into a real call site, on exactly the argument that makes `on:click={inc}` one. Before this, `$effect(fn)`, `$effect.pre(fn)`, `$effect.root(fn)`, `$effect.untracked(fn)` and `$derived.by(fn)` all emitted NOTHING: the js delegate correctly suppresses the rune itself, but the argument is an ordinary identifier and no edge was made for it, so a component's own graph could not show that it runs `fn` on every effect tick. THE SET IS THE INVOKING HALF of the rune surface — $effect, $effect.pre, $effect.root, $effect.untracked, $derived.by, $host — and that split IS the ruling, not an implementation detail. The value-taking runes ($derived(count), $state(0), $state.raw(v), $bindable(v), $props(), $inspect(v), $effect.tracking()) hand over something that is never called, so an edge there would point a call at an expression; the read is already a `uses` edge, so refusing the call loses no data flow. Pinned by `svelte/rune-invocations` and the mutant `svelte/rune-invocation-dropped`, which removes only rune-pass edges so the js-delegate call inside `$effect(inlineCall())` and the D8 template-handler call both survive and a failure is attributable to this ruling rather than to the delegate. TWO SHAPES REMAIN SILENT BY DESIGN: an arrow argument is not a name and its body is already walked, and a member argument ($effect(obj.m)) names a method this lane does not resolve. A user's own `$`-prefixed function is not a rune — the same reason `isRuneCallee` refuses a bare `$` prefix. OBSERVED, NOT CHANGED: a downstream dedupe collapses repeated (source, target, type) pairs to one edge, so two runes invoking the SAME function leave a single row and the other call site becomes invisible. That is pre-existing shared behaviour across relationship types, it is why the fixture gives every call site a distinct callee, and it is left alone here rather than fixed inside a contract ruling — but it is a real loss of call-site resolution and belongs on the list with the `#914` residual and the go separator retraction.

decisions.node_type: template-side calls: on:click={inc}, on:submit={() => save()}, on:click={box.open}, {@render row(it)}
decisions.question: Do template event handlers and render tags produce call relationships?
decisions.ruling: YES (0.85 usage_contextual) — the template pass emits them via pure-String scanning of opaque svelte_raw_text attribute values (bare identifier / first ident-then-paren / dotted callable leaf) and render_tag opaque-text scan (0.9). The embedded-JS oracle cannot see template constructs; the F5 oracle now derives the SAME truth from the template tree. fixture: template-calls (pins inc/save/open/row).
decisions.resolution: RULED — YES, call edges, current behaviour ratified (2026-09-27). A template event handler and a render tag are call sites: `on:click={inc}`, `on:submit={() => save()}`, `on:click={box.open}` and `{@render row(it)}` all emit `calls`, and a dotted target resolves to its LAST segment — verified at three depths (`box.open`->open, `helpers.row`->row, `box.deep.fn`->fn), which also closes the D4 note that render tags and `on:` handlers used to answer the same shape in opposite directions. The arrow-param form (`on:click={(e) => ...}`) emits nothing, because an arrow is not a name. CROSS-FAMILY DISAGREEMENT, recorded rather than smoothed over: the sibling vue lane emits NO calls for its equivalents — `@click="inc"` and `@submit="save()"` both produce nothing, and only `uses` edges for a receiver or a collection. So the two SFC siblings now differ on this ruling and on nothing else measured. Vue's silence has the shape of the same under-claim, and it is NOT changed from this lane: vue is not svelte's to edit, and the parallel to the cross-lane gap X1 (a javascript-owned defect found from here and deliberately not fixed here) is exact. If the family wants them aligned, that is a separate ruling against the vue lane. Pinned by `svelte/rune-invocations` (the handler row) plus the pre-existing `svelte/template-calls`, `svelte/onclick-handler-lines` and the `svelte/render-first-segment-calls` / `svelte/drop-on-handler-calls` mutants.

decisions.node_type: HTML builtin tag set drift (analyzer vs F5 oracle)
decisions.question: Can <search> (2023 HTML element) or camelCase SVG tags surface as component instantiates?
decisions.ruling: NO — HTML_BUILTIN_TAGS covers all 134 modern-HTML + SVG tags; the F5 oracle's ORACLE_HTML_TAGS drifted (126 tags, missing search + 7 SVG camelCase) and faked a MISSING instantiates->search in vue-element-admin. Lesson (family-wide): parallel builtin lists on analyzer and oracle sides must be diffed by a set-comparison probe, not trusted. fixture: vue/modern-html-svg-builtin-tags (forbids search + 7 SVG tags).

decisions.question: M49 W13 (W12 residual): the analyzer's H2 rule emits `instantiates X` when a `<svelte:component this={X}/>` target is an import-bound bare identifier, but the oracle's component-usage walk skipped `svelte:component` as a builtin tag - and the dynamic target is named by an ATTRIBUTE, so the tag-name walk never saw it either. The analyzer's correct edge therefore surfaced as the one unexplained edge W12's 400-file svelte measurement left open (corpus file: packages/svelte/tests/runtime-legacy/samples/event-handler-shorthand-dynamic-component/main.svelte).
decisions.decision: RULED - the oracle mirrors the analyzer's gate and nothing more: `deriveSvelteComponentUsages(root, importBindings)` emits `instantiates` for a bare-identifier `this={X}` when X is an import binding. The analyzer's second gate (skip a target that resolves to a declared member, which carries a `uses` edge instead) is deliberately NOT mirrored: an ES module cannot both import and declare the same name, so an import-bound name can never trip it and a non-import name is rejected by the import gate. Measured: the bindings are NOT available from the embedded-script truth (probed - `deriveTreeEdges(st, "javascript")` emits zero edges for `import Widget from './Widget.svelte'`), so they are walked off the JS-parsed script tree, mirroring the analyzer's `imports[].items`. Per-file parity on the real corpus file: analyzer `instantiates|Widget` vs oracle `instantiates|Widget`, 0 missing / 0 unexplained; lane re-run at 60 files svelte 100%/0/0, javascript 744/744, typescript 100%, baseline gate no regressions. Pinned by F9-PROBE-SVELTE-DYNAMIC-COMPONENT (both directions asserted, so the mirror cannot trade an unexplained edge for a fabricated one) and proven load-bearing by revert; the analyzer side was already pinned by fixture svelte/relationship-kinds.
